analysis:
Examined all supplied units.

- Test goldens: gemma-4-26b.json head line 1 adds a routedExperts field (loadedBytes 24265359360, 128 experts, 8 selected). expected.json lines 46-48, 67-69 and 88-90 update the plan/handoff SHA256 values for the three Gemma 4 pair plans. These are test fixtures, not runtime trust anchors.
- Main.swift head line 66 adds the checkGemmaRoutedExperts test call. Its implementation was not supplied.
- Submodule: libs/mlx-swift-lm moves 7933a0f -> 3c01ffc. Its contents are not supplied, so this is a coverage limit. The inference engine (TB-007) and the KV/batch decode arithmetic (Gemma4BatchDecodeScope, Gemma4BatchArithmeticAgreement) live there. Cross-request state isolation under batching (T-028/T-041) depends on that unseen code.
- DistributedInstalledPlan.swift (head ~332-336, 360-370): defaultBatchLanes now takes prefillSchedule. A Gemma 4 layer-stage pipeline with serial prefill and no private images defaults to 4 lanes instead of 1. The one-chunk lookahead schedule, or a nil schedule, keeps the old default.
  - This raises default concurrency for coordinator-registered pairs and so widens the multi-tenant co-residency surface: concurrent requests from different consumers share the batch.
  - The comments claim each decode row keeps one-request arithmetic, lanes are charged their whole request state per rank, and admission is checked against live memory.
  - Environment overrides and the malformed-override-to-1 behavior appear unchanged.
- No concrete regression is shown in the visible code. Risks to verify:
  - Per-lane KV and request isolation in the submodule: no cross-request leakage between lanes (T-028, A-001).
  - Cancellation and joining paths for Gemma multi-lane. The base comment said multi-lane qualification was pending; the head comment exempts Gemma serial pipelines (T-010 availability).
  - Memory-admission refusal behavior for DoS.
- Integration should confirm that Gemma4BatchDecodeScope's per-lane cache separation and the qualification evidence exist in the submodule diff.
